student_passage:
Four friends in our class wanted to put on a short show, but we had no costumes. Our teacher placed a lamp behind a white sheet. (1) ____ We decided to tell a story using the dark shapes instead of dressing up.

At first, each person tried to move a different paper animal at once. Nobody could follow the story. (2) ____ After this new plan, the audience saw only one character at a time, and the speaker had time to say its name.

A thin paper bird kept bending and falling. Holding it closer to the lamp did not help. (3) ____ With the stronger piece, it stood straight, so we could move it across the sheet without stopping the story.

We all knew the words in our story well. Each child read the lines live and listened for a cue. (4) ____ The others waited for that final word before moving their figures. We did not need recorded music.

During the last practice, nobody turned the lamp on. We had all thought it was someone else's job. (5) ____ The next day, we wrote everyone's job on paper and tested the show quietly before the visitors came.

completed_passage:
Four friends in our class wanted to put on a short show, but we had no costumes. Our teacher placed a lamp behind a white sheet. She showed us how our hands could make shapes on the sheet. We decided to tell a story using the dark shapes instead of dressing up.

At first, each person tried to move a different paper animal at once. Nobody could follow the story. We agreed to let only one paper animal appear at a time. After this new plan, the audience saw only one character at a time, and the speaker had time to say its name.

A thin paper bird kept bending and falling. Holding it closer to the lamp did not help. We cut another bird from a thicker card. With the stronger piece, it stood straight, so we could move it across the sheet without stopping the story.

We all knew the words in our story well. Each child read the lines live and listened for a cue. A familiar word at the end of one line was the signal for the next person. The others waited for that final word before moving their figures. We did not need recorded music.

During the last practice, nobody turned the lamp on. We had all thought it was someone else's job. We needed a list of jobs, not just another practice of the story. The next day, we wrote everyone's job on paper and tested the show quietly before the visitors came.
